summary: An excerpt from a science fiction novel (Book 15, part 159) set aboard an interstellar ship bound for New Holyoke. Ray Marlowe talks with Rich Becker, who suspects the enemy Lilaikens have access to too much classified intelligence and may be manipulated. Becker suggests that if Ray can prove Whiston financial backing of the Lilaiken movement, he could be either decorated or have his career ruined. Ray then reflects on canceled plans with Emma, whom Frederick Whiston forbade from attending a pre-deceleration party, and his own feelings of childishness. Kilgore then appears, changing into shore-leave clothes.
one_line: Ray Marlowe talks with Becker about suspected intelligence manipulation by the Lilaikens, while Emma's date is canceled aboard ship before New Holyoke.
key_facts: Becker tells Ray that the bad guys seem to have access to entirely too much classified intelligence, which he says smells like manipulation.
Ray has given the Lilaikens plenty of reasons to want him out of the way, according to Becker's dialogue.
Becker says that if Ray proves Whiston financial backing of the Lilaiken movement, someone will either give him a very impressive medal or hang his career out to dry.
Becker shrugs noncommittally and leaves the room after saying it was good work all the same.
Ray was supposed to have a last shipboard date with Emma that included dinner and the theatre, then a run up to the obs platform to see New Holyoke.
The entertainment director's flier described the obs platform view of New Holyoke as breathtaking.
Emma called Ray late in the morning to cancel the date, sounding distinctly unhappy and almost tearful.
Frederick forbade Emma from leaving, saying the last night before hard deceleration is a raucous, crass and demeaning scene.
Ray suspects Frederick is hypocritical about orgies and wants to protect little sister's virtue.
Ray expects to be on New Holyoke for months, possibly years, if the EED does not get a handle on the Lilaikens.
Ray believes he will still see Emma on the ground, since she has promised to tour Blackheath Grange with him.
Kilgore emerges from the short hallway leading back to the bedroom, half dressed and buttoning his shirt.
Kilgore has changed into Marine-on-shore-leave attire, a loud shirt and tough khaki cargo pants.
